predictions.question: The first relay used 'truly unclamped' as its baseline, which conflates two things the clamp does: writing the ring's forty held values, and re-solving Vmem for the WHOLE tissue a second time every hold iteration (a side effect of how embryo.py implements the Gpol clamp, not a spatial signal from the ring). Direct counterfactuals already showed these interact (+0.148 ring alone, +0.010 update alone, +0.366 together, a +0.207 interaction) and that R1 in the first relay found the ring's own conductance pulling AGAINST selectivity (-0.273) while the update carried +0.639. This isolates the ring's held VALUES specifically, against a baseline that already gets the tissue-wide re-solve, so the only remaining difference is what is actually written on the ring.
predictions.registeredBefore: any state from the new baseline was computed or looked at. The updated causal predictions (R2'-R5') are informed by the FIRST relay's already-published, registered results (a legitimate prior update, not a peek at this run); B1 and B2 are new and were reasoned from the lattice's shell structure alone.
predictions.baseline: extraUpdateOnly: every hold iteration gets the tissue-wide second Vmem update (ionCurrent + gapCurrent re-solved for every cell), but the ring's G_pol is never overwritten -- it is left to whatever the normal, clipped update computes. This is boundaryHarmonicStep.Step with ringHeld=False, extraUpdate=True during the hold. The trained run is unchanged: ringHeld=True, extraUpdate=True, identical to the actual trained model.
predictions.method: identical to the first relay (data/boundaryHarmonicRelayPredictions...json): D(n) = trained(n) - baseline(n), D(n+1) = Jbar(n) D(n) + src(n) exactly, src(n) now measuring only the ring overwrite (both conditions already include the tissue-wide re-solve, so it cancels out of src). Same validity gates.
predictions.geometry: shellCells(s) in boundaryCodeUtilities, s=0 (the 40-cell ring) to s=5 (cell 60, the nose's centre). Eyes and mouth sit at shell 2; the nose spans shell 4 (cells 49, 71) and shell 5 (cell 60) -- it is the deepest feature, consistent with the field screen's blind spot found earlier. shellDepth-weighted mean position at time n: sum_i |value_i(n)| * shell(i) / sum_i |value_i(n)|, over all 121 cells.

V1.criterion: worst one-step residual <= 1e-6; every readout's flux conserved to <= 1e-3 after the hold

V2.claim: the shares read as a flow, not cancellation
V2.criterion: cancellation index <= 5 at release, trough and peak

R1.claim: isolating the ring leaves almost nothing else to attribute the gap to
R1.criterion: ring conductance accounts for >= 95% of the source flux (this is a check that the new baseline removed the confound, not a substantive causal claim)

R2.claim: even the ring's own isolated effect has already left the ring by release
R2.criterion: ring share of the selectivity gap at release <= 10% (replicating the first relay's finding, now with the confound removed)

R3.claim: handover to the interior is rapid, not during a later selective rise
R3.criterion: the interior's share overtakes the ring's within 20 iterations of release

R4.claim: the nose fills no earlier than the eyes, by the flux-based half-time
R4.criterion: nose half-time (as in the first relay) is >= eyes half-time

R5.claim: the relay still runs mainly through the field, not gap junctions
R5.criterion: field channel carries >= 50% of gross transferred flux, release to peak

B1.claim: RAW imprint (|D|, no downstream weighting): the ring's effect lingers near the boundary before penetrating to the nose's depth, rather than moving straight in
B1.criterion: the |D|-weighted mean shell depth is <= 1.5 during the first third of the clear phase (release to trough) and exceeds 3.0 during the final third

B2.claim: the same lingering pattern holds for the part of the imprint that actually matters for the readout (the selectivity flux), not just the raw deviation
B2.criterion: same two checkpoints (<=1.5 first third, >3.0 final third) using the selectivity flux in place of |D|

predictions.diagnostics: reported without a registered threshold: the full shellDepth(t) curve for both |D| and flux, release to peak, plotted directly -- a genuine outward bounce (a local rise in depth after an earlier fall) would be visible there even though B1/B2 only test for delayed penetration, not a literal reversal.
